Rashi on Chullin 25a:10:1.hebrew: אמר קרא וכל כלי פתוח - דמדאדכר פתיחה בכלי חרס, קאמר וכתיב "הוא", למימרא דהאי הוא דתלייה רחמנא בצמיד פתיל, מכלל דאינך אפילו יש צמיד פתיל עליהן טמאין, אלמא מגבן נטמאו:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:10:1.english: The verse says: "And every open vessel" - Since [the verse] mentions an opening in connection with an earthenware vessel, it says, and it is written, "hu" ["it [is unclean]"]. This means that it is only this one [the earthenware vessel] that the Merciful One made dependent on a tight-fitting cover; by implication, the others, even if there is a tight-fitting cover on them, are impure. Evidently, they become impure from their outer sides.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:12:1.hebrew: גולמי - שלא נגמרה כל מלאכתן, כדמפרש ואזיל, אבל נגמרה חקיקתן וראויין הן לתשמישן:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:12:1.english: Unfinished [vessels] - Whose work was not entirely completed, as [the Gemara] explains as it continues, but their carving was completed and they are fit for their use.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:12:2.english: Their flat ones - Even if their work was completed.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:12:3.hebrew: טהורין - דאיתקש עץ לשק, דכתיב (ויקרא יא) "מכל כלי עץ או בגד או עור או שק": מה שק מטלטל מלא וריקן, אף כל מטלטל מלא וריקן:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:12:3.english: Are pure - For wood is compared to sackcloth, as it is written (Leviticus 11) "of any vessel of wood, or garment, or skin, or sack": just as a sack is carried both full and empty, so too everything [that is susceptible to impurity as a vessel] must be carried both full and empty.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:12:4.hebrew: גולמי כלי מתכות טהורין - ולקמן מפרש טעמא:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:12:4.english: Unfinished metal vessels are pure - And later [the Gemara] explains the reason.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:12:5.hebrew: פשוטיהן טמאין - אם נגמרה כל מלאכתן. דכלי מתכות לא איתקוש לשק, וטומאת כלי מתכות כתוב בפרשת מדין (במדבר לא): אך את הזהב ואת הכסף וגו':
Rashi on Chullin 25a:12:5.english: Their flat forms are impure - If all their work was completed. For metal vessels were not compared to sackcloth, and the impurity of metal vessels is written in the passage about Midian (Numbers 31): "Only the gold and the silver, etc."

Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:1.hebrew: לשוף - לשפשף בדבר המחליקן ומצחצחן, כמו שעושין בעשב שקורין אשפריל"א:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:1.english: To polish - To rub with something that smooths and scours them, as is done with the grass that is called *espril* (horsetail/scouring rush).

Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:2.hebrew: לשבץ - לשון משבצות. מרמצן עשויין כמזלגים קטנים, כמו "ומפקי ליה ברמצא דפרזלא" במסכת נדה (דף סב.). כלומר, שמחוסרין לתקוע בהן מסמרות ומשבצות לנוי, כמו שעושים בארגז הנשים:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:2.english: To set in settings - It is an expression of settings (*mishbetzot*). *Marmatzan* are made like small forks, as in "and they take it out with an iron *ramtza*" in tractate Niddah (page 62a). That is to say, they still lack having nails and decorative settings fixed into them, as is done to a women's chest.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:3.english: To scrape - With a rahitna [a carpenter's planing tool], to smooth.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:4.hebrew: לכרכב - שחוקק בהן חקיקות גדולות וכרכוב, כדרך שעושים בכיסוי תיבות וספסלים:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:4.english: To make a rim - That he carved large carvings and a molding into them, as is done on the lids of chests and on benches.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:5.hebrew: להטיח בטונס - דג הוא, כמו ששנינו באלו טרפות (לקמן חולין סו:): אפונס ואטונס ושפין בעורו כלי עץ להחליק, וכדאמר בסנהדרין (דף כ:): משישפשף בעור הדג:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:5.english: To rub with a tunas - It is a fish, as we learned in [the mishna of] "These are the terefot" (later, Chullin 66b): "[The fish called] afunas, atunas, and shafin [are used to] rub wooden vessels with their skin, to smooth them." And as it says in Sanhedrin (20b): "From when he rubs it with fish skin."

Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:6.hebrew: או שמחוסר כן - בסיס לישב עליו:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:6.english: Or that it lacks a stand - A base upon which to sit.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:7.hebrew: אוגן - שפה לפיו, כמו שעושין לכלי ששותין בו יין לנוי:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:7.english: A rim - A lip at its mouth, like what is made for a vessel from which one drinks wine, for decoration.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:8.hebrew: אוזן - אנש"א בלע"ז, כמו שעושין לקופה ולנפה:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:8.english: Handle - *Anse* in Old French, like what is made for a basket and for a sieve.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:9.hebrew: מחוסר חטיטה - טהור, דלאו כלי הוא:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:13:9.english: Lacking carving out - It is pure, because it is not [yet] a vessel.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:14:1.hebrew: דחק קפיזא בקבא - כלי שבדעתו לחוק עד שיחזיק קבא, חקק בו ג' לוגין. ואע"פ שראוי למלאכה, הואיל ולשם קב התחיל בו ודעתו להשלימו, לא הוי גמר מלאכה:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:14:1.english: He hollowed out a kapiza, [intending it to hold] a kav - A vessel that he intends to hollow out until it holds a kav; he hollowed out three log in it. And even though it is [already] fit for use, since he began it for the sake of [making it hold] a kav and he intends to complete it, it is not considered a completed work.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:1:1.hebrew: ואפילו מלא חרדל - שהכלי אינו נוגע בכולו, אלא במה שסמוך לדפנות, והאמצעיים מיטמאין מן האויר. ואי אתה יכול לומר שזה מטמא את זה, שהרי אין כביצה בכל אחד; ועוד, אין אוכל מטמא אוכל; ועוד, אם כן זה שני וזה שלישי, והשלישי לא יעשה רביעי לטמא את האמצעיים:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:1:1.english: And even if it is full of mustard - For the vessel does not touch all of it, but only what is adjacent to the walls, and the middle ones become impure from the air. And you cannot say that this one renders that one impure, since there is not an egg-bulk in each one; and furthermore, food does not render food impure; and furthermore, if so, this one is second-degree and that one is third-degree, and the third-degree would not produce a fourth-degree to render the middle ones impure.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:2:1.hebrew: ויהא כלי חרס מיטמא מגבו - בנגיעה:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:2:1.english: And let an earthenware vessel become impure from its outer side - By contact.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:2:2.english: By a kal vachomer - Since its inside is revealed to you by the verse, which is not the case with other vessels, and its outer side [becomes impure] through contact, let it come by a kal vachomer: Just as a kli shetef, which does not become impure through its airspace without contact, as [the Gemara] derives later from "its inside" – the inside of this one and not the inside of another...

Rashi on Chullin 25a:2:3.hebrew: מיטמאין מגבן - בנגיעה, כדכתיב (ויקרא יא) וכל אשר יפול עליו וגו', עליו משמע דנגע, ולא שנא גבו ולא שנא אוירו:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:2:3.english: Become impure from their outer surface - By contact, as it is written (Leviticus 11): "And anything upon which [any of them] falls..." "Upon it" implies that it touched [it], and it makes no difference whether [it touched] its outer surface or its airspace.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:3:1.hebrew: כלי פתוח - מדקפיד אפתיחה, שמע מינה בכלי חרס קאי. דאיזהו כלי שטומאתו קודמת לפתחו? באיזה כלים הרגילה תורה את הטומאה להשכים ולמהר ולבא דרך פתחו:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:3:1.english: An open vessel - Since [the verse] is particular about the opening, learn from this that it refers to an earthenware vessel. For which is the vessel whose impurity precedes its opening? In which vessels did the Torah accustom the impurity to arrive early and quickly, and to enter through its opening?

Rashi on Chullin 25a:3:2.hebrew: הוי אומר זה כלי חרס - דכתב לך בגויה בדוכתא אחריתי: "אל תוכו":
Rashi on Chullin 25a:3:2.english: Say, then, that this is an earthenware vessel - For [the Torah] wrote for you, regarding an earthenware vessel, in another place: "into its interior."

Rashi on Chullin 25a:3:3.hebrew: הא יש צמיד פתיל עליו - שמצומדת מגופתו עליו, לפיו יפה:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:3:3.english: But it has a tightly bound cover on it - Since its lid is joined to it, on its mouth, well.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:3:4.english: A cord - [It must be made] from the vessel itself.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:3:5.hebrew: טהור - ואף על פי שהוא באהל המת, דקרא באהל המת מישתעי, אלמא לא נטמא מגבו:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:3:5.english: Pure - Even though it is in a tent with a corpse, [it remains pure], since the verse is speaking of [a vessel] in a tent with a corpse. Evidently, it does not become impure from its outer surface.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:4:1.hebrew: ומה כלי חרס שאין מיטמא מגבו - כדאמרן:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:4:1.english: If an earthenware vessel, which does not become impure from its outer surface - As we said.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:6:1.hebrew: הא דרשינהו - חד לגופיה וחד לגזירה שוה דנאמר "תוכו" לטמא כו':
Rashi on Chullin 25a:6:1.english: But these "its inside" [verses] have already been expounded - One is for its own matter, and one is for the verbal analogy, as it is stated "its inside" to render impure, etc.:

Rashi on Chullin 25a:7:1.hebrew: ארבעה קראי כתיבי - תרי "תוכו", ובכל חד הוה מצי למיכתב "תוך", וכתב "תוכו":
Rashi on Chullin 25a:7:1.english: Four verses are written - [There are] two [instances of] "its inside," and in each one [the Torah] could have written "inside," yet it wrote "its inside."

Rashi on Chullin 25a:8:1.hebrew: חד לגופיה - תוך האמור לטמא לגופיה אתא, שיטמא הכלי כל אוכלין ומשקין שבאוירו, אע"פ שלא נגע:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:8:1.english: One for its own matter - The word "its inside" that is stated regarding rendering impure comes for its own matter: that the vessel renders impure all foods and liquids that are in its airspace, even though they did not touch it.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:8:2.hebrew: וחד לג"ש - ללמוד על הכלי שיקבל טומאה מן האויר אע"פ שלא נגע בו השרץ, כדאמרינן לעיל (חולין דף כד:): נאמר "תוכו", לטמא כו':
Rashi on Chullin 25a:8:2.english: And one for a gezera shava - To teach about the vessel, that it receives impurity from the air even though the creeping creature did not touch it, as we said above (Chullin 24b): It is stated "its inside," to render impure, etc.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:8:3.hebrew: תוכו ולא תוך תוכו ואפילו כלי שטף מציל - אם היה כלי מונח בתוך כלי חרס, ופי הפנימי למעלה מפי החיצון, כדמפרש בתורת כהנים, ואוכלים ומשקין בפנימי, וטומאה באויר החיצון, אין האוכלין טמאין, דלאו תוכו דכלי חרס נינהו אלא תוך תוכו. ואפילו כלי שטף מציל. ולא מיבעיא פנימי אם גם הוא של חרס דמציל, דכיון דאינו מיטמא מגבו לא נטמא וחוצץ בפני הטומאה שבאויר החיצון, אלא אפילו כלי שטף דמיטמא מגבו, ואיכא למימר לא יחוץ בפני הטומאה, מציל על האוכלין שבתוכו, שהרי גם הוא לא נטמא וחוצץ. דאי משום דנגע בחיצון, חיצון ראשון הוא, ואין כלי מקבל טומאה אלא מאב הטומאה. ואי משום דקאי באויר כלי חרס, וכתיב "וכל אשר בתוכו יטמא", ה"מ אוכלין ומשקין, אבל כלים אין מיטמאין. דתניא בפסחים (דף כ.) יכול יהו כל הכלים מיטמאין מאויר כלי חרס, ת"ל "כל אשר בתוכו יטמא", וסמיך ליה "מכל האוכל אשר יאכל", אוכל ומשקין מיטמאין מאויר כלי חרס, ואין כל הכלים מיטמאין מאויר כלי חרס:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:8:3.english: Its inside, but not the inside of its inside; and even a vessel that can be immersed [kli shetef] protects - If a vessel was placed inside an earthenware vessel, and the opening of the inner one was higher than the opening of the outer one, as explained in the Torat Kohanim, and there were foods and liquids in the inner vessel, and impurity was in the airspace of the outer vessel, the foods are not impure, since they are not the "inside" of the earthenware vessel but the inside of its inside. And even a vessel that can be immersed protects. It is not necessary to say that the inner vessel protects if it too is earthenware: since it does not become impure from its outer side, it did not become impure, and it acts as a barrier against the impurity in the airspace of the outer vessel. Rather, even a kli shetef, which does become impure from its outer side, and one might have said that it would not act as a barrier against the impurity, protects the foods inside it, since it too did not become impure and acts as a barrier. For if [one were to say it is impure] because it touched the outer vessel, the outer vessel is a first-degree impurity, and a vessel receives impurity only from a primary source of impurity [av hatumah]. And if [one were to say it is impure] because it stood in the airspace of an earthenware vessel, and it is written, "and all that is in it shall be impure," that applies only to foods and liquids, but vessels do not become impure. For it was taught in Pesachim (20a): One might think that all vessels become impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel; therefore the verse states, "all that is in it shall be impure," and it is adjacent to "of all the food which may be eaten." Foods and liquids become impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel, but not all vessels become impure from the airspace of an earthenware vessel.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:8:4.hebrew: כלי שטף - כל שאר כלים שאינם כלי חרס מיקרו כלי שטף, על שם שיש להם טהרה במקוה:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:8:4.english: Vessels of rinsing - All other vessels that are not earthenware vessels are called "vessels of rinsing," because they have purification in a mikveh.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:9:1.hebrew: אלא מתוכן ובנגיעה - עד שיפול לתוכן ויגע בהן. ונימא דהאי "אשר יפול עליו" על שוליו ועל דופנותיו מתוכו קאמר:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:9:1.english: Rather, from their inside and by contact - Until it falls into their inside and touches them. And let us say that this [phrase] "upon which it falls" refers to its base and its sides, from the inside.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:9:2.hebrew: מק"ו ומה כלי חרס שמיטמא מאוירו - בלא נגיעה:
Rashi on Chullin 25a:9:2.english: [It follows] a fortiori: Just as an earthenware vessel, which becomes impure from its airspace - Without contact.

Rashi on Chullin 25a:9:3.hebrew: אין מיטמא מגבו - אפילו בנגיעה כו':
Rashi on Chullin 25a:9:3.english: It does not become impure from its outer side - Even through touching, etc.

Tosafot on Chullin 25a:13:1.hebrew: להטיח בטונס - הקשה ר"ת, דבפ' שני דסנהדרין (ד' כ:) אמר, כלי עץ מאימתי מקבלים טומאה? העריסה והמטה, משישופם בעור הדג. ותירץ, דשיפה דהתם היינו להסיר את הקסמים הגדולים שמזיקין לישב עליה; אבל שפייה דהכא אינה אלא לנוי בעלמא, להחליקו ולצחצחו:
Tosafot on Chullin 25a:13:1.english: To plaster with tunas - Rabbeinu Tam asked: But in the second chapter of Sanhedrin (20b) it says: From when do wooden vessels become susceptible to impurity? A cradle and a bed, from when one has rubbed them with fish skin. And he answered: The rubbing there is to remove the large splinters, which are harmful to sit upon; but the rubbing here is only for mere decoration, to smooth it and polish it.

Tosafot on Chullin 25a:2:1.hebrew: (לעיל) ומה כל הכלים שאין מיטמאין מאוירן כו' - וא"ת, מה לכל הכלים, שכן נעשו אב הטומאה? ובסמוך נמי דעבד ק"ו איפכא, שיהו כל הכלים מיטמאין מאויר, איכא למיפרך: מה לכלי חרס, שכן אין לו טהרה במקוה? וי"ל, דלאו מכח כלי עביד ק"ו, אלא מכח גב ואויר. ומיהו, למאי דפרישית לעיל דהאי ק"ו הוי כמו "מה מצינו", דלא תקשה כל חד וחד תיקום אדוכתיה, קשה, דבמה מצינו ליכא למילף ליתן האמור של זה בזה, דאיכא למיפרך כדפרישית. ויש לומר כדפרישית לעיל, שיש כאן שום סברא לעשות ק"ו אחד יותר מאחר. ועוד, האי ק"ו דהכא לא נקטיה כלל אלא לרווחא דמילתא, דבסתם כלים כתיב טומאת מגע, אף מגבן, "וכל הכלי אשר יגע בו הזב יטמא", דמהיכא נמעט כלי חרס; ולשאר כלים דילפינן טומאת אויר מק"ו, היינו מכח גב ואויר, ולהכי איצטריך "תוכו" של זה ולא תוכו של אחר:
Tosafot on Chullin 25a:2:1.english: (Above) "And if all [other] vessels, which do not become impure through their airspace, etc." - But one may ask: what [proof is there] from all [other] vessels, seeing that they were made a primary source of impurity (avi ha-tum'ah)? And in the next [passage] too, where [the Gemara] makes the *kal va-chomer* in reverse, [arguing] that all vessels should become impure through airspace, one can refute: what [proof is there] from an earthenware vessel, seeing that it has no purification in a mikveh? And one can answer that [the Gemara] does not make the *kal va-chomer* on the strength of [the nature of] the vessel, but on the strength of the outer surface and the airspace. However, according to what I explained above, that this *kal va-chomer* is like a "what do we find" (mah matzinu) [argument], such that [the principle] "every one stands on its own" (kol chad ve-chad tekum ad-vokhtei) does not pose a difficulty, it is difficult, for with a "what do we find" [argument] one cannot derive by placing what is stated of this one onto that one, because one can refute it, as I explained. And one can say, as I explained above, that here there is some reasoning to make one *kal va-chomer* [stronger] than the other. Furthermore, this *kal va-chomer* here [the Gemara] did not mention at all except for added clarity, since with regard to vessels in general, impurity through contact is written—even from their outer surface: "and any vessel that the zav touches shall become impure"—for from where would an earthenware vessel be excluded? And as for other vessels, whose airspace impurity we derive from a *kal va-chomer*, this is on the strength of the outer surface and the airspace; and therefore [the word] "its inside" (tokho) of this one, and not the inside of another, was needed.

Tosafot on Chullin 25a:3:1.hebrew: איזהו כלי שטומאתו קודמת לפתחו הוי אומר זה כלי חרס - אבל אי לא כתיב "פתוח", ע"כ הוה מוקמינן ליה בכל הכלים, ולא הוה ידעינן מאי למידרש מהוא:
Tosafot on Chullin 25a:3:1.english: "Which vessel is it whose impurity precedes its opening? You must say: this is an earthenware vessel" - But if "open" were not written, we would necessarily have interpreted it as referring to all vessels, and we would not have known what to derive from the word "it" (hu).

Tosafot on Chullin 25a:4:1.hebrew: ויהיו כל הכלים מיטמאין מאוירן מק"ו - ואם תאמר, אם כן לא ליטמא מגבו, דהשתא מיתוקמא בכולהו קרא דכל כלי פתוח, דבכולם טומאה קודמת לפתחן? וי"ל דמ"מ לא מוקמינן ליה אלא בכלי חרס, דכתיב ביה טומאת אויר בהדיא:
Tosafot on Chullin 25a:4:1.english: And let all vessels become impure through their airspace, by a kal va-chomer - And if you say: If so, [the vessel] should not become impure from its outer side, for now the verse "any open vessel" is established with regard to all of them, since in all of them impurity precedes their being opened? And one can answer that in any case we only establish it [as referring] to an earthenware vessel, regarding which airspace impurity is written explicitly:

Tosafot on Chullin 25a:8:1.hebrew: וחד לגזירה שוה - מופנית היא, דהוה מצי למכתב "וכל אשר יפול מהם", "בו", "כל אשר בו":
Tosafot on Chullin 25a:8:1.english: And one for the verbal analogy (gezerah shavah) - It is superfluous (mufnit), for [the verse] could have written, "And anything that falls from them," "into it," [or] "anything that is in it."

Tosafot on Chullin 25a:8:2.hebrew: ואפילו כלי שטף מציל - פירש בקונטרס דלא מיבעיא כלי חרס דאין מיטמא מגבו, אלא אפילו כלי שטף דמיטמא מגבו מציל, שגם כלי שטף אינו מקבל טומאה מאויר כלי חרס, כדאמרינן בפסחים (דף כ.). וקשה לפירושו, דאם כן מה חידוש יש בכלי שטף יותר מבכלי חרס? ועוד, דאיכא חידוש יותר בכלי חרס מבכלי שטף, כגון אם שרץ באויר כלי חרס פנימי ואוכלין בכלי חרס חיצון, דטהור אף ע"פ שהפנימי טמא, דהוי רבותא טפי מבכלי שטף דאינו מקבל טומאה מאויר. ונראה לפרש דקרא אצטריך לכלי שטף, אף על גב דלאו מיניה הוא מחריב ביה; אבל כלי חרס דמיניה הוא, בלאו קרא ידעינן דחוצץ ומחריב ביה. וכן מוכח בשמעתא קמייתא דזבחים (דף ג:), דפריך ומי אמר רבא חטאת ששחטה על מי שמחוייב חטאת פסולה, על מי שמחוייב עולה כשרה; אלמא דמינה מחריב בה, דלא מינה לא מחריב בה, ותנן אפילו כלי שטף מציל, ומשני התם גלי קראי דארבעה תוכו כתיבי:
Tosafot on Chullin 25a:8:2.english: And even a vessel that is susceptible to impurity through immersion (keli shetef) protects - Rashi explained: It is not necessary [to state this] regarding an earthenware vessel, which does not become impure from its outer surface (gav); rather, even a keli shetef, which does become impure from its outer surface, protects, for even a keli shetef does not receive impurity from the airspace of an earthenware vessel, as we say in Pesachim (20a). But according to his explanation this is difficult: if so, what novelty is there in a keli shetef more than in an earthenware vessel? Moreover, there is a greater novelty in an earthenware vessel than in a keli shetef, for example, if a creeping creature (sherets) is in the airspace of an inner earthenware vessel and one eats [food] in an outer earthenware vessel, it is pure even though the inner one is impure; this is a greater novelty than in a keli shetef, which does not receive impurity from airspace. And it seems to explain that the verse was needed for a keli shetef, even though it is not made of the same material (lit. "from it"), [and yet] it destroys it (mecharev bo); but an earthenware vessel, which is made of the same material, we know even without a verse that it interposes and destroys it. And so it is proven in the first chapter of Zevachim (3b), where it asks: But did Rava say that a sin-offering (chatat) slaughtered for the sake of one who is obligated in a sin-offering is invalid, [but] for the sake of one who is obligated in a burnt-offering (olah) is valid? Evidently, that what is of its own material destroys it, [but] what is not of its own material does not destroy it; yet we learned [in the Mishnah], "even a keli shetef protects," and it answers: There, the verses reveal that "its inside" (tocho) is written four times:
